thread:
sam: noticing hosted p99 climb ~02:08 UTC, from ~120ms -> ~420ms. Dash shows queue depth spiking on gpu-pool-7.
maya: saw that too. p95 also up but p99 is wild. any deploys around then? :thinking:
deploy-bot: canary deploy completed: model-runtime/aux-kernels v2.3 -> v2.4 at 02:05 UTC by ci/cd
igor: linking kernel selector logs now. quick grep shows selector using AUX kernel on ~37% of requests starting 02:06.
sam: paste of selector summary:
```
[02:06:12] kernel_selector: sample window=60s total=124k choose_aux=37% choose_core=63%
[02:06:12] reason_breakdown: seq_len>1024: 22%, kv_miss: 11%, cold_start:4%
```
luis: interesting — aux kernel latency higher for short seqs (there's a kernel mismatch). profile from one worker:
```
worker-17 profile: aux_v2 p50=110ms p95=380ms p99=620ms
worker-17 profile: core_v1 p50=95ms p95=140ms p99=210ms
```
maya: that aligns — if selector misroutes short/kv-hit traffic to aux, p99 explodes.
ryan: any tenant correlation? ops-bot: top tenants by requests during spike: tenant-17 (20%), tenant-3 (12%), tenant-internal-batch (9%). tenant-17 traffic is lots of short completions.
sam: looks like coalescer/batching sampler might be favoring larger batches and pushing small fast requests into aux path. can we confirm sampler weights?
igor: sampler config at commit 4f3a shows sampler_threshold_ms=40 and batch_pad_mode=prefer_large (recent change in v2.4).
luis: prefer_large + kernel selector heuristics = bad combo for mixed workloads.
maya: rolling a quick config revert to prefer_small for pool-7? risk: throughput drop for large seqs.
sam: do it for canary first (pool-7 canary subsets). Who's oncall to push config? @ryan
ryan: i'll do canary revert now. pushing config: 
```
kubectl -n runtime set configmap sampler-config pool-7 --from-literal=batch_pad_mode=prefer_small
```
ryan: applied to canary subset at 02:22. monitoring...
deploy-bot: config rollout to canary subset completed at 02:23 UTC
sam: early signals: p99 on canary workers dropped from ~620ms -> ~170ms within 30s.
maya: nice. global pool still noisy; we should stage rollback to remaining nodes if stable for 10m.
igor: collecting kernel selector traces to postmortem; saving sample traces (selector decisions + seq_len + kv_hit).
luis: action items: (1) revert batch_pad_mode for pool-7 (handled canary) (2) adjust selector heuristics to penalize aux for seq_len<256 or kv_hit=true (3) add a canary test that mimics mixed small/large seq traffic.
maya: + add metric alert for aux selection ratio > 20% for pools serving >10k req/min.
ryan: will escalate to rollout team if canary stable at 10m. current canary window 6m and stable.
ops-bot: alert suppressed for p99-hosted for pool-7 (auto-suppress due to active remediation) at 02:29 UTC
sam: thanks team. Igor, please attach the selector traces to the incident ticket and I'll draft a short postmortem entry.
igor: will attach. quick note — root cause: recent patch changed sampler bias and combined with selector heuristics created a routing path that favored an aux kernel with worse latency for short/kv-hit work. regressions in config combo, not single kernel.
luis: propose followup: add an integration test that runs mixed seq distribution against kernel selector and sampler in staging.
maya: agreed. closing loop after global rollback.
ryan: global revert in progress 02:35 -> 02:41 UTC, p99 back to baseline by 02:40 on most pools.
sam: closing thread once postmortem is filed. :white_check_mark:
